items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1958-07-18
items.q: you take a guy like Mel Powell, Teddy Wilson, everything, you like to play it up

ctx.x: Let me see if there's another question about, well when you were a first boy, first started to learn when you were a boy, about how long did you play though, even when you fooled around with it yourself, even if you didn't take regular lessons, how would you advise, say somebody wanted to learn to play three or four hours, would that be too much a day, or what would you think would be a bit higher than the practice of play on the instrument?

Oh yeah, well you got to practice because it's mostly your finger to exercise, you know what I mean? You got to develop your fingers just like, just like any other ones. You got to practice. Because I remember now, I tell you, like I used to play in a band, see like a dance band. They don't just play for dancing, so you never get a chance to win, we'd get with a small combination, they play something real fast. You know, and you got to wake into that too, to get used to playing things fast. A lot of time, you…
Well it usually comes to you. Did you have quite a little time to get your fingers more fast? Yeah.

items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: I never could play nothing fast until I got with Terry Wilson started picking up that fast because he played piano and you know he'd feature in the band

ctx.x: Could you beat off some about the right tempo for them as fast as they played?

Well now? In the old days? In the old days everything was, every, the hard, let's see, was it. Like Tiger Rags, for instance? Tiger Rags was about the fastest thing they would play. How would they stop it off? It wasn't too fast. But now today I just pick up that, I never could play nothing fast until I got with Terry Wilson started picking up that fast because he played piano and you know he'd feature in the band, he liked everything up, you know. So I got so used to that and all.

I was going to ask again about the Alberts system. They don't have as many keys usually as the BAME. Do you think that makes it easier to slide from one note to the other by not having too many rings and keys? Or do you like to have as many keys and rings as possible on it? No, I'm making slurs, Bill. Yeah, like when you, you know, I mean does it seem more like a vocal quality to you? Can you do more with it as far as the fingering, the extra keys that the game has, do they hold you back with your finger? What,…
